edition: The State of Mental Health in America 2025 (report PDF dated 2025/09). The MHA landing page on 2026-10-03 is titled 'The State of Mental Health in America 2025' and its ranking guidelines are '2025 Ranking Guidelines'; no 2026 edition was linked.
ranking_text: States with positive outcomes are ranked higher (closer to one) than states with poorer outcomes (closer to 51). The overall, adult, youth, prevalence, and access rankings were analyzed by calculating a standardized score (Z score) for each measure and ranking the sum of the standardized scores. The majority of measures represent data collected up to 2023. An overall ranking of 1-13 indicates lower prevalence of mental illness and higher rates of access to care; 39-51 indicates higher prevalence and lower rates of access. The combined scores of all 17 measures make up the overall ranking.

measure_sources.mha_adult_ami_pct: SAMHSA, Center for Behavioral Health Statistics and Quality, National Survey on Drug Use and Health (state releases); MHA text: 'In 2022 and 2023, the most recently available state-level data'
measure_sources.mha_youth_mde_pct: SAMHSA NSDUH state releases; youth ages 12-17; MHA text refers to 2022-2023
measure_sources.mha_youth_mde_no_services_pct: SAMHSA NSDUH; MHA text: 'In 2022-2023 combined data, over half (50.80%) of youth (ages 12-17) with a major depressive episode (MDE) did not receive any treatment or counseling for depression in the past year ... In Alabama (ranked 51) nearly two-thirds of youth with MDE did not receive treatment in 2022-2023.'
measure_sources.mha_adult_ami_uninsured_pct: SAMHSA NSDUH; MHA text: 'In 2022-2023, 9.20% of adults with any mental illness (AMI) in the U.S. were uninsured'
measure_sources.mha_mh_workforce_ratio: County Health Rankings and Roadmaps (National Provider Identification data file); MHA text: 'In 2024, there were 320 individuals for every one mental health provider in the U.S.'

notes: Tables were read from the HTML of the ranking pages (fetched same-origin and parsed in the browser). Rank tables have 51 rows (50 states + DC); measure tables have an extra 'National' row. MHA's page text for AMI also quotes a 2024 national figure (23.40%), which differs from the National row of the state table (22.95%, 2022-2023). MHA workforce ratio for Alabama (740:1) is a rounded figure from an older CHR release than the CHR values in this dataset (684:1 in CHR 2025 annual; 639:1 in the March 2026 supplement).
